name: SpaceGenes+
tagline: Interactive dashboard showing how radiation and microgravity together affect astronaut health at the molecular level.
problem: Astronauts experience radiation and microgravity at the same time, but most space omics tools study each stressor in isolation, hiding interactions that matter for long-duration missions.
solution: A web dashboard that ingests NASA GeneLab transcriptomic data (OSD-288, mouse spleen in spaceflight), computes synergy scores from fold changes across radiation-only, microgravity-only and combined conditions, and flags genes whose combined response exceeds the sum of the individual effects, for researchers, drug developers and mission planners.

why_it_stood_out.claim: Won the award for the best and most valid use of science and/or the scientific method.
Gives researchers and mission planners an easy way to identify important molecular changes for long-duration spaceflight protection.
Flips the usual framing: existing tools treat spaceflight stressors separately, while the product looks for non-additive effects of combined stress.
The science is explicit and checkable: one named GeneLab dataset and a stated synergy rule (combined effect greater than the sum of single effects).
A one-person entry used no-code and AI-assisted tools for speed while keeping dataset choice and synergy logic explicit, so tool leverage did not cost validity.

lessons: Narrow a broad challenge to the one question a named user (a mission planner) must answer.
State the dataset and the rule behind every result; validity judges reward science they can check.
No-code and AI tools are fine when the disclosure says exactly what each did.

sources.note: Team-written summary, method, tools, AI-use disclosure and NASA data.
